description: Films whose running time is 112 minutes or more are included; a film of exactly 112 minutes counts.

c.request: Using 112 minutes (`film.length`) as the cutoff for a long film and considering only the long films, for each language (`film.language_id`) give the language id, the average replacement cost (`replacement_cost`), and the average running time, ignoring missing values in each average (missing if none remain). Sort by average running time from highest to lowest, with missing averages last, show the top 10, and don't round. Films whose running time is 112 minutes or more are included; a film of exactly 112 minutes counts.
c.sql:
SELECT f.language_id, AVG(f.replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(f.length) AS avg_running_time
FROM film AS f
WHERE f.length >= 112
GROUP BY f.language_id
ORDER BY avg_running_time IS NULL, avg_running_time DESC
LIMIT 10;

d.request: For films with a running time of at least 112 minutes, group by language ID and return the language ID, average replacement cost, and average running time, ignoring NULL values separately in each average; sort by average running time descending with NULL averages last, return the top 10, and do not round.
d.sql:
SELECT language_id, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(length) AS avg_running_time
FROM film
WHERE length >= 112
GROUP BY language_id
ORDER BY avg_running_time IS NULL, avg_running_time DESC
LIMIT 10;

a.request: Looking only at films whose running time (`film.length`) is at least 112 minutes, for each language (`film.language_id`) give the language id, the average replacement cost (`replacement_cost`), and the average running time, ignoring missing values in each average (missing if none remain). Sort by average running time from highest to lowest, with missing averages last, show the top 10, and don't round.
a.sql:
SELECT f.language_id, AVG(f.replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(f.length) AS avg_running_time
FROM film AS f
WHERE f.length >= 112
GROUP BY f.language_id
ORDER BY avg_running_time DESC
LIMIT 10;

b.request: For films with `film.length >= 112`, group by `film.language_id` and return the language ID, the average non-missing `replacement_cost`, and the average non-missing `length`; sort by average length descending with missing averages last, return the top 10, and do not round.
b.sql: SELECT language_id, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(length) AS avg_length FROM film WHERE length >= 112 GROUP BY language_id ORDER BY avg_length IS NULL, avg_length DESC LIMIT 10;
